This lets you add an icon to your enum's value in the intellisense.

CommandEnumNameAttribute

This lets you change the name the user needs to type for that value. By default, it will convert the names to snake_case.

CommandEnumRegistry

This is a registry for command enums, it lets you hold enum values, their icons, change and register them. This is what you use to make them available for command arguments of type enum. Soft enums are suggested values that can be added to at runtime, they don't have to be predefined and the user doesn't have to put one of those values. Enums are values that are predefined (you can change them later by re-registering the enum) and the user has to pick one of those values, nothing else.

CommandEnumRegistry.EnumValue

The value type for enums, having the icon and the actual int value.

CommandEnumRegistry.SoftEnumValue

The value type for a soft enum, having the icon and the actual value string.

CommandEnumTypeNameAttribute

You should probably not use this but if you do then fair enough I guess. This is to have the parser link the original enum type name to this parameter.

CommandNbtTagTypeAttribute

Metadata for the parser to know what types to allow.

CommandOverload

Represents a specific overload of a command, defining its parameters and their types.

CommandParserMetadataAttribute

This is an attribute that will be given to the parser as metadata. This is essentially a base attribute type that tells it what to collect.

CommandPathAttribute

This lets you attach a path to a parameter, specifically a string. It's kind of like an enum, but the command can only execute if the name matches. This is useful for subcommands. This goes on a string and will always contain the path's name in the parameter as it's the only option that will be allowed to be called. Different overloads can have different path values, keeping only the ones that match the input. See the command guide if it's still unclear, basically it's selecting one value of an 'enum', not any others.

CommandPosition

Represents a position that can be absolute or relative.

OnixCommandBase

The base class for all commands. You should inherit from this class to create your own commands. You should mark overload methods with the OnixCommandBase.OverloadAttribute attribute for them to be called.

OnixCommandBase.OverloadAttribute

This is the attribute you need to put on your function for it to be considered.

OnixCommandBase.RawStringAttribute

This marks this string parameter as a raw string. This must be the last parameter, it will eat the whole input. (it was hungry.)

OnixCommandBase.SoftEnumNameAttribute

This lets you attach a soft enum to a string parameter.

OnixCommandOrigin

Wraper around the origin of a command getting run. When you check IsInWorld, you can assume World, Dimension and Region are not null. When you check IsEntity, you can assume Entity, World, Dimension and Region are not null. When you check IsClientSide, you can run client specific code.
